questions.q: Who received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award announced in September 2026?
questions.x: The award for 2024, for Kannada cinema. Mohanlal got it for 2023.

questions.q: Who received the 60th Jnanpith Award?
questions.x: R. Vairamuthu (Tamil). The 59th went to Vinod Kumar Shukla.

questions.q: "The End of Everything", Booker Prize 2026 winner, was written by…
questions.x: M. John Harrison, the oldest Booker winner at 81.

questions.q: Tommy Koh, a 2026 Ramon Magsaysay awardee, is from which country?
questions.x: 2026 awardees: Tommy Koh (Singapore), Runa Khan (Bangladesh), Bo Kyi (Myanmar).

questions.q: How many Padma awards were announced for 2026?
questions.x: 5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri.

questions.q: Which country hosted World Environment Day 2026?
questions.x: 2026: Azerbaijan. 2025: Republic of Korea. 2024: Saudi Arabia.

questions.q: What was the theme of World Water Day 2026?
questions.x: 2026: Water and Gender. 2025: Glacier Preservation. 2024: Water for Peace.

questions.q: "Planet vs. Plastics" was the Earth Day theme of which year?
questions.x: 2024. The 2025 theme was "Our Power, Our Planet".

questions.q: What was the World Health Day 2026 theme?
o: Together for health. Stand with science.
questions.x: Observed on 7 April, WHO's founding day (1948). 2025: Healthy beginnings, hopeful futures; 2024: My health, my right.

questions.q: The UN declared 2026 the International Year of the…
questions.x: 2026: Woman Farmer (also Rangelands and Pastoralists, and Volunteers). 2025: Glaciers, Cooperatives, Quantum Science. 2023: Millets.

questions.q: World Wetlands Day 2026 linked wetlands to…
questions.x: Observed on 2 February, the day the Ramsar Convention was signed (1971).

questions.q: Exercise Dharma Guardian is held between India and which country?
questions.x: Dharma Guardian = India–Japan army exercise. The 7th edition (2026) was in Uttarakhand. Asked in 2021 and 2025.

questions.q: Who became India's Chief of Defence Staff in May 2026?
questions.x: He is the 3rd CDS, after Bipin Rawat and Anil Chauhan.

questions.q: Who is the present Chief of the Air Staff?
questions.x: Ashutosh Dixit became the 29th CAS on 31 October 2026, after A.P. Singh.

questions.q: KHANJAR 2026, held at Misamari in Assam, is an exercise with…
questions.x: KHANJAR = India–Kyrgyzstan special forces (13th edition, February 2026). Kazakhstan = Prabal Dostyk; Uzbekistan = Dustlik.

questions.q: AUSTRAHIND is a military exercise between India and…
questions.x: India–Australia. The 5th edition was in Kerala from 19 October 2026.

questions.q: Pralay, tested again in November 2026, is what type of missile?
questions.x: Pralay is a DRDO quasi-ballistic surface-to-surface missile, tested from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha.

questions.q: INS Aridhaman is India's ___ nuclear ballistic-missile submarine.
questions.x: Arihant (1st) → Arighaat (2nd) → Aridhaman (3rd), all Arihant class.

questions.q: The Navy's "Operation Urja Suraksha" (2026) was linked to…
o: Escorting ships through the Strait of Hormuz crisis
questions.x: It protected India's oil and gas shipping during the 2026 Hormuz crisis.

questions.q: SAREX-2026, the 12th National Maritime Search and Rescue Exercise, was held off…
questions.x: Organised by the Indian Coast Guard off Paradip in October 2026.

questions.q: After the RBI's October 2026 policy, the repo rate is…
questions.x: Raised by 25 basis points; stance "calibrated tightening". Re-check after the 4 December 2026 review.

questions.q: The fiscal deficit target in Budget 2026-27 is…
questions.x: 4.3% for 2026-27. The 2025-26 estimate was 4.4%.

questions.q: The new GDP series released in February 2026 uses which base year?
questions.x: Base year changed from 2011-12 to 2022-23. CPI's new base is 2024.

questions.q: Who chairs the 16th Finance Commission?
questions.x: Arvind Panagariya. It keeps the states' share of central taxes at 41% for 2026-27 to 2030-31. N.K. Singh chaired the 15th.

questions.q: The law that replaced MGNREGA (December 2025) guarantees how many days of work?
questions.x: The VB–G RAM G Act raised the guarantee from 100 to 125 days.

questions.q: What is the reference date for Census 2027 in most of India?
questions.x: 1 March 2027 (00:00 hours). Snow-bound areas of Ladakh, J&K, Himachal and Uttarakhand use 1 October 2026.

questions.q: India signed a free trade agreement with which country on 27 April 2026?
questions.x: New Zealand. Oman CEPA was December 2025; the UK deal July 2025.

questions.q: Which site became India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2026?
questions.x: Inscribed at the Busan session, July 2026.

questions.q: How many Ramsar sites does India have (October 2026)?
questions.x: The newest include Sukhna (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (UP).

questions.q: India's 58th tiger reserve is…
questions.x: Madhav (MP), which now has 9 tiger reserves. Ratapani was the 57th.

questions.q: Which Odisha nesting beach did NOT see mass nesting of olive ridleys in 2026?
o: None — all three had mass nesting
questions.x: Gahirmatha missed mass nesting in 2026. Rushikulya had mass nesting from mid-March.

questions.q: What is the size of Odisha's 2026-27 budget?
questions.x: Presented on 20 February 2026 by CM Mohan Charan Majhi.

questions.q: Odisha's "Mission PoWaR" stands for…
questions.x: Power, Water and Roads for every revenue village.

questions.q: The 600 MW Upper Indravati pumped-storage project is in which district?
questions.x: At Ranibahal in Kalahandi; approved on 9 November 2026.

questions.q: Who won the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025 for Odia?
questions.x: For the poetry book Padapurana; announced March 2026.

questions.q: Odisha's 2026 semiconductor MoU was with Intel and which company?
questions.x: About US$3.3 billion for a glass substrate facility.

questions.q: After the 2026 amendment, how many judges can the Supreme Court have besides the CJI?
questions.x: 37 + CJI = 38 in all (earlier 33 + CJI). Parliament fixes the number by law under Article 124(1).

questions.q: Which state's name was changed in the Constitution in August 2026?
questions.x: Kerala became Keralam by a law under Articles 3–4, not by an amendment under Article 368. Orissa became Odisha in 2011.

questions.q: Who became Chief Minister of West Bengal in May 2026?
questions.x: Suvendu Adhikari formed the first BJP government in West Bengal.

questions.q: V.D. Satheesan became Chief Minister of which state in 2026?
questions.x: Kerala; the Congress-led UDF government was sworn in on 18 May 2026.

questions.q: Who is the present Chief Justice of India?
questions.x: Justice Surya Kant, the 53rd CJI, serves till 9 February 2027.

questions.q: India's rank in the Global Peace Index 2026?
questions.x: 127th of 163. Iceland is first.

questions.q: India's rank in the Global Hunger Index 2026?
questions.x: 100th of 122, score 24.1 ("serious").

questions.q: Who publishes the Global Innovation Index?
questions.x: WIPO. India was 38th of 139 in 2026; Switzerland is first.

questions.q: India's rank in the 2026 World Press Freedom Index?
questions.x: 157th of 180, published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF).

questions.q: Which satellite was lost when PSLV-C62 failed in January 2026?
questions.x: DRDO's EOS-N1 plus 15 co-passengers, lost to a third-stage problem.

questions.q: Besides three Americans, which country's astronaut flew on Artemis II?
questions.x: Jeremy Hansen of Canada, around the Moon in April 2026.

questions.q: Who won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize?
questions.x: Navi Pillay (South Africa). 2025: María Corina Machado; 2024: Nihon Hidankyo; 2023: Narges Mohammadi.

questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Medicine was for which technique?
questions.x: Optogenetics: Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel.

questions.q: Whom did India beat in the 2026 men's T20 World Cup final?
questions.x: By 96 runs at Ahmedabad, 8 March 2026.

questions.q: Who won the FIFA World Cup 2026?
questions.x: Spain beat Argentina 1–0 after extra time.

questions.q: What was India's rank at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi–Nagoya?
questions.x: 85 medals, 21 gold.

questions.q: Which Indian city will host the 2030 Commonwealth Games?
questions.x: Ahmedabad. The 2026 Games were in Glasgow.

questions.q: When was the 18th BRICS summit held in New Delhi?
questions.x: It ended with the New Delhi Declaration.

questions.q: Which city hosted the 26th SCO summit in 2026?
questions.x: Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, marking 25 years of the SCO. The 25th (2025) was in Tianjin, China.

questions.q: COP31 was held in…
questions.x: Antalya, 9–20 November 2026. Ethiopia (Addis Ababa) is expected to host COP32.

questions.q: Which Central Asian country won a UN Security Council seat for the first time in June 2026?
questions.x: Kyrgyzstan, for 2027–28.

questions.q: Which country holds the G20 presidency in 2026?
questions.x: The USA; the summit is in Miami in December 2026.

questions.q: In the 2026 BRICS theme, what does the "B" stand for?
questions.x: Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.

questions.q: Who became Prime Minister of Nepal in March 2026?
questions.x: Balendra Shah of the Rastriya Swatantra Party, the first Madhesi PM.

questions.q: Tarique Rahman became Prime Minister of which country in 2026?
questions.x: Bangladesh (BNP), sworn in on 17 February 2026.

questions.q: Viktor Orbán lost power in Hungary in 2026 to…
questions.x: Péter Magyar of the Tisza party won the 12 April 2026 election.

questions.q: The Strait of Hormuz lies between which two countries?
questions.x: It links the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman.

questions.q: Which country brokered the April 2026 US–Iran ceasefire?
questions.x: A two-week truce from 8 April 2026.

questions.q: Exercise Shakti is held between India and which country?
questions.x: Shakti = India–France (army). Indra = Russia; Mitra Shakti = Sri Lanka; Garuda Shakti = Indonesia.

questions.q: Which military exercise does India hold with Nepal?
questions.x: Surya Kiran = Nepal. Sampriti = Bangladesh; Hand-in-Hand = China; Nomadic Elephant = Mongolia.

questions.q: Which four countries take part in the Malabar naval exercise?
questions.x: Malabar began as India–USA in 1992; Japan joined permanently in 2015 and Australia in 2020 (the Quad countries).

questions.q: Who was India's first Chief of Defence Staff?
questions.x: Bipin Rawat (from 1 January 2020). Then Anil Chauhan, and from May 2026 N.S. Raja Subramani.

questions.q: Which is the oldest paramilitary force of India?
questions.x: Assam Rifles, raised in 1835 as the Cachar Levy.

questions.q: Which force guards India's borders with Nepal and Bhutan?
questions.x: SSB guards Nepal and Bhutan. ITBP = China; BSF = Pakistan and Bangladesh; Assam Rifles = Myanmar.

questions.q: Which Army rank is equal to a Wing Commander in the Air Force?
questions.x: Wing Commander = Lt Colonel = Commander (Navy). Squadron Leader = Major; Group Captain = Colonel.

questions.q: Which is the highest peace-time gallantry award?
questions.x: Ashoka Chakra (peace time). Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime award.

questions.q: Where is the Indian Naval Academy?
questions.x: Ezhimala in Kannur district, Kerala.

questions.q: The BrahMos missile is made by India with which country?
questions.x: BrahMos = Brahmaputra + Moskva. It is a supersonic cruise missile.

questions.q: What kind of missile is Akash?
questions.x: Akash is a medium-range surface-to-air missile. Nag is anti-tank; Astra is air-to-air; Prithvi is surface-to-surface.

questions.q: Which was India's first home-built aircraft carrier?
questions.x: INS Vikrant, built at Cochin Shipyard, commissioned in September 2022. Vikramaditya was bought from Russia; Arihant is a submarine.

questions.q: Operation Sindoor (May 2025) was…
o: India's strikes on terror camps in Pakistan after the Pahalgam attack
Navy anti-piracy mission in the Red Sea
Relief mission after an earthquake in Myanmar
questions.x: Strikes on terror camps in Pakistan and PoK after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack. Sudan evacuation was Operation Kaveri; Myanmar relief was Operation Brahma.

questions.q: Where is the National Defence Academy?
questions.x: NDA is at Khadakwasla. IMA is in Dehradun; Defence Services Staff College at Wellington.

questions.q: Exercise Desert Flag is hosted by…
questions.x: The UAE hosts Desert Flag at Al Dhafra air base.

questions.q: Which deficit shows the total borrowing needs of the government?
questions.x: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure minus total receipts other than borrowing. It equals how much the government must borrow.

questions.q: Fiscal deficit minus interest payments is called…
questions.x: Primary deficit removes interest on old loans, so it shows the borrowing for this year's spending alone.

questions.q: The Monetary Policy Committee of the RBI has how many members, and who heads it?
questions.x: Six members: three from the RBI and three appointed by the government. The RBI Governor chairs it and has a casting vote.

questions.q: What is the RBI's inflation target?
questions.x: 4% CPI inflation, with a tolerance band of 2% to 6%.

questions.q: Which price index does the RBI use for its inflation target?
questions.x: Since 2014–16 the RBI targets headline CPI (combined) inflation.

questions.q: Who issues the one-rupee note?
questions.x: The one-rupee note is issued by the Ministry of Finance and signed by the Finance Secretary. All other notes are issued by the RBI.

questions.q: GST started on ___, and the GST Council is under Article ___.
questions.x: GST came on 1 July 2017 through the 101st Amendment. Article 279A sets up the GST Council; 246A gives the power to make GST laws.

questions.q: Which Five Year Plan was based on the Mahalanobis model?
questions.x: The Second Plan (1956–61) followed P.C. Mahalanobis and stressed heavy industry. The First Plan used the Harrod–Domar model.

questions.q: Which was the last Five Year Plan?
questions.x: The 12th Plan ended in 2017. NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.

questions.q: Who is the chairperson of NITI Aayog?
questions.x: The Prime Minister chairs NITI Aayog. The Vice-Chairperson and CEO run it day to day.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a dimension of the Multidimensional Poverty Index?
questions.x: The MPI uses three dimensions: health, education and standard of living. It does not use income.

questions.q: Which committee is linked to banking sector reforms?
questions.x: The Narasimham Committees (1991 and 1998) recommended banking reforms. Tendulkar and Rangarajan worked on poverty lines; Kelkar on taxes.

questions.q: Disguised unemployment means…
o: More people work than needed, so removing some does not reduce output
People are out of work only in some seasons
People lose jobs because of new technology
People change jobs and are briefly without work
questions.x: Disguised unemployment is common in farming: the extra workers add nothing to output. Seasonal, technological and frictional unemployment are the other options.

questions.q: What is the minimum amount for an RTGS transfer?
questions.x: RTGS needs at least ₹2 lakh and has no upper limit. NEFT has no minimum.

questions.q: Which body regulates pensions in India?
questions.x: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority runs the NPS. IRDAI regulates insurance; SEBI regulates markets.

questions.q: Who coined the word "ecosystem"?
questions.x: Arthur Tansley in 1935. Haeckel coined "ecology".

questions.q: The zone where two ecosystems meet, like a mangrove between land and sea, is called…
questions.x: An ecotone is a transition zone. It often has more species than either side (edge effect).

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of India's four biodiversity hotspots?
questions.x: India's four hotspots: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats–Sri Lanka and Sundaland (Nicobar).

questions.q: What is the IUCN Red List status of the olive ridley turtle?
questions.x: The olive ridley is Vulnerable. In India it is in Schedule I of the Wildlife Act.

questions.q: Which law is called the umbrella law for the environment in India?
questions.x: It was passed after the Bhopal gas tragedy and gives the Centre wide powers.

questions.q: Which protocol protects the ozone layer?
questions.x: Montreal phases out ozone-depleting gases. Kyoto = greenhouse gases; Cartagena = biosafety; Nagoya = benefit sharing.

questions.q: Which convention deals with wetlands?
questions.x: Ramsar (Iran), 1971. Bonn = migratory species; CITES = trade in wildlife; Basel = hazardous waste.

questions.q: By which year does India aim to reach net-zero emissions?
questions.x: Announced at COP26 in Glasgow (2021) as part of the Panchamrit.

questions.q: COP30 was held in ___, and COP31 in ___.
questions.x: COP30: Belém, Brazil (2025). COP31: Antalya, Türkiye (November 2026). COP29 was Baku; COP28 Dubai.

questions.q: Where is the head office of the UN Environment Programme (UNEP)?
questions.x: UNEP is in Nairobi, Kenya. The UNFCCC secretariat is in Bonn.

questions.q: The build-up of a poison at higher levels of the food chain is called…
questions.x: Biomagnification: e.g. DDT becomes more concentrated in birds of prey than in the fish they eat.

questions.q: As of October 2026, how many Ramsar sites does India have?
questions.x: 103 Ramsar sites, and 58 tiger reserves.

questions.q: Which country hosted World Environment Day 2025?
questions.x: 2025: Republic of Korea. 2024: Saudi Arabia. 2026: Azerbaijan. 2023: Côte d'Ivoire.

questions.q: Which gas is the main human-made cause of the greenhouse effect?
questions.x: CO₂ contributes the most to human-caused warming, mainly from burning fossil fuels.

questions.q: Which was India's first biosphere reserve?
questions.x: Nilgiri, 1986, across Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka.

questions.q: Who is called the father of civil services in India?
questions.x: Lord Cornwallis (Governor-General 1786–93) organised and reformed the civil services.

questions.q: Who called the All India Services the "steel frame" of India?
questions.x: Sardar Patel defended the All India Services in the Constituent Assembly and called them the steel frame.

questions.q: Who was the first Indian to join the Indian Civil Service?
questions.x: Satyendranath Tagore, elder brother of Rabindranath, qualified in 1863.

questions.q: Which committee designed the prelims–mains–interview pattern of the civil services exam?
questions.x: The D.S. Kothari Committee (1976) recommended the three-stage exam, used from 1979.

questions.q: In which year was the first Public Service Commission set up in India?
questions.x: The Public Service Commission was set up in 1926 on the advice of the Lee Commission (1924).

questions.q: Under the RTI Act, a reply normally must be given within how many days?
questions.x: 30 days. If the life or liberty of a person is involved, it must be given within 48 hours.

questions.q: The Citizens' Charter idea began in which country?
questions.x: It began in Britain in 1991 under PM John Major.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three parts of the Sevottam model?
questions.x: Sevottam has three parts: Citizens' Charter, grievance (complaint) handling and service delivery capability.

questions.q: Who coined the word "Lokpal"?
questions.x: Dr L.M. Singhvi coined "Lokpal" and "Lokayukta" in 1963.

questions.q: Who chaired the 2nd Administrative Reforms Commission?
questions.x: The 2nd ARC (2005) was chaired by M. Veerappa Moily. The 1st ARC (1966) was chaired first by Morarji Desai, then K. Hanumanthaiya.

questions.q: In the JAM trinity, what does "M" stand for?
questions.x: JAM = Jan Dhan (bank account), Aadhaar (identity) and Mobile, used for direct benefit transfer.

questions.q: When was Digital India launched?
questions.x: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015.

questions.q: When is Civil Services Day observed?
questions.x: 21 April, the day in 1947 when Sardar Patel addressed the first batch of officers.

questions.q: Which commission said Governors should be non-partisan persons from outside the state?
questions.x: The Sarkaria Commission (1983–88) on Centre–State relations.

questions.q: Which Article lets Parliament create a new All India Service?
questions.x: Article 312, after the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution with a two-thirds majority.

questions.q: Who was the first Governor-General of India (not of Bengal)?
questions.x: The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India; William Bentinck was the first. Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal.

questions.q: Who was the first Viceroy of India?
questions.x: After the Government of India Act 1858, Lord Canning became the first Viceroy.

questions.q: Which Viceroy is called the father of local self-government in India?
questions.x: Lord Ripon's resolution of 1882 laid the base for local self-government.

questions.q: The Vernacular Press Act was passed by ___ and repealed by ___.
questions.x: Lord Lytton passed the "gagging Act" in 1878; Lord Ripon repealed it in 1882.

questions.q: Which Act brought dyarchy in the provinces?
questions.x: The 1919 Act (Montagu–Chelmsford reforms) split provincial subjects into reserved and transferred. The 1935 Act brought dyarchy at the Centre.

questions.q: Which Act first gave separate electorates to Muslims?
questions.x: The Morley–Minto reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

questions.q: What is called the Magna Carta of English education in India?
questions.x: Charles Wood's Despatch of 1854 laid out education from primary school to university.

questions.q: Who started the Mahalwari system of land revenue?
questions.x: Holt Mackenzie, 1822. Cornwallis brought the Permanent Settlement (1793); Munro and Read the Ryotwari system.

questions.q: Who was the first woman president of the Indian National Congress?
questions.x: Annie Besant (Calcutta, 1917). Sarojini Naidu (Kanpur, 1925) was the first Indian woman president.

questions.q: Who led the 1857 revolt at Jagdishpur in Bihar?
questions.x: Kunwar Singh, then about 80 years old, led the revolt in Bihar.

questions.q: Who founded the Servants of India Society in 1905?
questions.x: Gokhale founded it in Pune in 1905 to train people for national service.

questions.q: Who edited the newspaper Al-Hilal?
questions.x: Maulana Azad started Al-Hilal in 1912. Mohammad Ali edited Comrade.

questions.q: Which was Odisha's first newspaper?
questions.x: Utkal Dipika was started in 1866 by Gourishankar Ray at Cuttack.

questions.q: Under which Viceroy was the shift of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi announced?
questions.x: It was announced at the Delhi Durbar of 1911, during Lord Hardinge's time.

questions.q: Which Congress session passed the resolution on Fundamental Rights?
questions.x: Karachi, 1931, presided by Sardar Patel. Lahore 1929 passed Purna Swaraj.

questions.q: Who was the first president of the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC)?
questions.x: Lala Lajpat Rai presided over AITUC's founding in 1920.

questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?
questions.x: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.q: Which Indian state touches three countries: Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan?
questions.x: West Bengal borders Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan. Sikkim touches Nepal, Bhutan and China.

questions.q: Which is the highest peak of South India?
questions.x: Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala's Anaimalai Hills. Doddabetta is the highest in the Nilgiris.

questions.q: Which is the highest peak fully inside India's administered territory?
questions.x: Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) on the Sikkim–Nepal border. K2 is higher but lies in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, which India claims.

questions.q: Which two big rivers flow west into the Arabian Sea through rift valleys?
questions.x: Narmada and Tapi flow west through rift valleys and form estuaries, not deltas.

questions.q: Where does the Narmada rise?
questions.x: Amarkantak in the Maikal Range. The Tapi rises at Multai, the Godavari at Trimbakeshwar, the Krishna at Mahabaleshwar.

questions.q: Which soil is best for cotton?
questions.x: Black soil holds moisture well, which suits cotton.

questions.q: The India State of Forest Report is published by ___ every ___.
o: Forest Survey of India; two years
Wildlife Institute of India; five years
questions.x: The Forest Survey of India, Dehradun, publishes it every two years.

questions.q: Which state has the largest forest area?
questions.x: Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest area. By percentage of its own area, Mizoram leads.

questions.q: In which state is the Nathu La pass?
questions.x: Nathu La in Sikkim links India with Tibet (China).

questions.q: The border line between India and China in the east is called the…
questions.x: The McMahon Line (1914). Durand Line = Pakistan–Afghanistan; Radcliffe Line = India–Pakistan/Bangladesh.

questions.q: Most of India's coal is found in which rock system?
questions.x: About 98% of India's coal is Gondwana coal, found in Damodar, Mahanadi and Godavari valleys.

questions.q: Kalbaisakhi storms are…
o: Violent April–May thunderstorms in Bengal and Odisha
Hot dry winds of north India in summer
questions.x: Kalbaisakhi or Nor'westers. Loo is the hot wind; mango showers are in Kerala/Karnataka; western disturbances bring winter rain.

questions.q: Which is the largest biogeographic zone of India?
questions.x: The Deccan Peninsula covers about 42% of India's area.

questions.q: The International Court of Justice has how many judges, and where does it sit?
questions.x: 15 judges with 9-year terms, at The Hague in the Netherlands.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a permanent member of the UN Security Council?
questions.x: The P5: USA, UK, France, Russia and China.

questions.q: Where is the head office of UNESCO?
questions.x: UNESCO is in Paris.

questions.q: Where is the head office of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)?
questions.x: FAO is in Rome, as are IFAD and the World Food Programme.

questions.q: How many members does NATO have now?
questions.x: Finland joined in 2023 (31st) and Sweden in 2024 (32nd).

questions.q: Which country joined ASEAN in 2025 as its 11th member?
questions.x: Timor-Leste became the 11th ASEAN member in October 2025.

questions.q: Where is the BIMSTEC secretariat?
questions.x: BIMSTEC is in Dhaka. The SAARC secretariat is in Kathmandu.

questions.q: Who publishes the Human Development Report?
questions.x: The UN Development Programme publishes the HDI every year.

questions.q: Who publishes the Global Gender Gap Report?
questions.x: The World Economic Forum (Geneva).

questions.q: Which became India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2026?
questions.x: Sarnath (2026). Maratha Military Landscapes were the 44th (2025); Moidams the 43rd (2024).

questions.q: Where was the 18th BRICS summit held?
questions.x: New Delhi, September 2026, under India's chairship. 17th: Rio (2025); 16th: Kazan (2024).

questions.q: Which country hosted the G20 summit in 2025?
questions.x: Johannesburg, South Africa, the first G20 summit in Africa. 2024: Brazil; 2023: India; 2026: USA.

questions.q: Where is the head office of the International Solar Alliance?
questions.x: Gurugram, India. The ISA was launched by India and France in 2015; IRENA is in Abu Dhabi.

questions.q: Which UN body has its head office in Nairobi?
questions.x: UNEP (and UN-Habitat) are in Nairobi. UNICEF = New York; WFP = Rome; UNHCR = Geneva.

questions.q: Which is the highest peak of Odisha?
questions.x: Deomali (1,672 m) in Koraput district.

questions.q: Which is the highest waterfall of Odisha?
questions.x: Barehipani in Similipal. Joranda is also in Similipal; Duduma is in Koraput; Khandadhar in Sundargarh.

questions.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake of Odisha?
questions.x: Ansupa in Cuttack district. Chilika is brackish (a lagoon).

questions.q: The Brahmani river is formed by the meeting of which two rivers?
questions.x: They meet at Vedavyas near Rourkela.

questions.q: Where does the Baitarani rise?
questions.x: Gonasika hills in Keonjhar district.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a mass nesting site of olive ridley turtles in Odisha?
questions.x: The three mass nesting (arribada) sites are Gahirmatha, the Rushikulya mouth and the Devi mouth.

questions.q: In which year was Chilika removed from the Montreux Record?
questions.x: Chilika was put on the Montreux Record in 1993 and removed in 2002 after the new sea mouth improved it.

questions.q: Which place in Odisha is famous for chromite?
questions.x: Sukinda (and Baula-Nuasahi). Panchpatmali = bauxite, Talcher = coal, Barbil = iron ore.

questions.q: Where is NALCO's bauxite mine?
questions.x: Panchpatmali hills in Koraput; the refinery is at Damanjodi and the smelter at Angul.

questions.q: Who led the Paika Rebellion of 1817?
questions.x: Bakshi Jagabandhu Bidyadhar led it in Khurda in 1817.

questions.q: Who founded the Utkal Sammilani in 1903?
questions.x: Madhusudan Das (Utkal Gourab) founded it to unite Odia-speaking areas.

questions.q: Where was the salt satyagraha held in Odisha?
questions.x: Inchudi in Balasore district, in 1930.

questions.q: Who was the first Chief Minister of Odisha after independence?
questions.x: Harekrushna Mahtab. Biswanath Das was Odisha's first Prime Minister (Premier) in 1937.

questions.q: Who built the Sun Temple at Konark?
questions.x: Narasimha Deva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty, 13th century. Chodaganga Deva began the Jagannath temple at Puri.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a Ramsar site of Odisha?
questions.x: Odisha's six Ramsar sites: Chilika, Bhitarkanika, Satkosia, Tampara, Hirakud and Ansupa.

questions.q: Who was the first Odia to win the Jnanpith Award?
questions.x: Gopinath Mohanty, 1973, for Mati Matala.

questions.q: Which Schedule of the Constitution has the anti-defection law?
questions.x: The 10th Schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment in 1985. It disqualifies a member who leaves the party they were elected from.

questions.q: The 6th Schedule covers tribal areas of which four states?
questions.x: 6th Schedule = autonomous district councils in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Tribal areas of other states fall under the 5th Schedule.

questions.q: Who called the Preamble the "identity card of the Constitution"?
questions.x: N.A. Palkhivala used this phrase. K.M. Munshi called the Preamble the "horoscope" of the Constitution.

questions.q: Which Article gives the right to go to the Supreme Court to protect Fundamental Rights?
questions.x: Article 32 (constitutional remedies). Ambedkar called it the heart and soul of the Constitution. Article 226 is the High Court's writ power.

questions.q: Who presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament?
questions.x: The President calls the joint sitting (Article 108), but the Lok Sabha Speaker presides over it.

questions.q: Within how many days must the Rajya Sabha return a Money Bill?
questions.x: The Rajya Sabha can only suggest changes and must return a Money Bill in 14 days; after that it is deemed passed.

questions.q: Which amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18?
questions.x: The 61st Amendment (1988, in force 1989) changed Article 326 to make the voting age 18.

questions.q: Which committee recommended adding Fundamental Duties?
questions.x: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976). The duties were added by the 42nd Amendment as Article 51A.

questions.q: Which Article mentions a Uniform Civil Code?
questions.x: Article 44 is a Directive Principle asking the State to try to secure a Uniform Civil Code. Article 40 is village panchayats.

questions.q: Members of a State Public Service Commission are appointed by ___ and removed by ___.
questions.x: The Governor appoints State PSC members, but only the President can remove them (Article 317).

questions.q: What is the term of the NHRC chairperson?
questions.x: After the 2019 amendment, the NHRC chairperson holds office for 3 years or until 70, whichever comes first.

questions.q: Which of these states does NOT have a Legislative Council?
questions.x: Six states have a Legislative Council: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka. Odisha has proposed one but it is not yet created.

questions.q: Which amendment gave one-third reservation to women in the Lok Sabha and Assemblies?
questions.x: The 106th Amendment (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023). It starts after the next census and delimitation.

questions.q: Financial Emergency is under which Article, and how many times has it been used?
questions.x: Article 360 is Financial Emergency. It has never been declared. Article 352 = National Emergency, 356 = President's Rule.

questions.q: Who decides whether a bill is a Money Bill?
questions.x: Under Article 110(3) the Lok Sabha Speaker's decision on a Money Bill is final.

questions.q: Weather and TV satellites usually use which orbit?
questions.x: A geostationary satellite stays over the same spot, so dishes don't need to move.

questions.q: Who was the first Indian to go to the International Space Station?
questions.x: Shubhanshu Shukla, on Axiom-4 in 2025. Rakesh Sharma (1984) went to the Soviet Salyut-7 station.

questions.q: Which rocket launched Chandrayaan-3?
questions.x: LVM3 (earlier called GSLV Mk III) launched it on 14 July 2023.

questions.q: National Space Day is observed on…
questions.x: 23 August, when Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's south pole in 2023.

questions.q: Which mosquito spreads dengue?
questions.x: Aedes spreads dengue, chikungunya and Zika. Anopheles spreads malaria; Culex spreads filaria and Japanese encephalitis.

questions.q: Lack of which vitamin causes scurvy?
questions.x: Vitamin C. D → rickets, B1 → beriberi, A → night blindness.

questions.q: Who discovered the germ that causes tuberculosis?
questions.x: Robert Koch, 1882. 24 March is World TB Day.

questions.q: LPG is mainly made of…
questions.x: LPG = propane + butane. CNG is mainly methane.

questions.q: National Science Day, 28 February, marks…
o: C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman effect
questions.x: Raman announced the effect on 28 February 1928.

questions.q: A scramjet engine works at…
questions.x: A scramjet needs air coming in at very high speed, so it works above Mach 5.

questions.q: Which mission made India the fourth country to dock two satellites in space?
questions.x: SpaDeX (Space Docking Experiment), docked in January 2025, after the USA, Russia and China.

questions.q: Who is the father of the Indian space programme?
questions.x: Vikram Sarabhai founded ISRO's forerunner INCOSPAR. Bhabha is the father of India's nuclear programme.

questions.q: In which layer of the atmosphere is the ozone layer?
questions.x: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere, about 15–35 km up.

questions.q: Which is the most variable gas in the atmosphere?
questions.x: Water vapour ranges from almost 0% in deserts to about 4% in humid tropics.

questions.q: Limestone changes into which rock under heat and pressure?
questions.x: Limestone → marble. Shale → slate, sandstone → quartzite, granite → gneiss.

questions.q: Which scale measures the damage caused by an earthquake?
questions.x: The Mercalli scale measures intensity (damage). The Richter scale measures the energy (magnitude).

questions.q: Which country has the most active volcanoes?
questions.x: Indonesia, on the Pacific Ring of Fire.

questions.q: India's only active volcano is…
questions.x: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea. Narcondam is dormant.

questions.q: Which ocean has the widest continental shelf?
questions.x: The Arctic Ocean, off Siberia.

questions.q: What are tropical cyclones called in the Philippines?
questions.x: Baguio in the Philippines; typhoon in China and Japan; willy-willy in Australia; hurricane in the Caribbean and USA.

questions.q: The Mistral is a cold wind that blows in…
questions.x: The Mistral blows down the Rhône valley in France. The Khamsin is in Egypt, the Foehn in the Alps, the Pampero in Argentina.

questions.q: What does El Niño usually do to India's monsoon?
questions.x: El Niño warms the eastern Pacific and usually weakens India's monsoon. La Niña usually strengthens it.

questions.q: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.x: Lake Baikal in Russia (about 1,640 m). The Caspian Sea is the largest lake by area.

questions.q: The temperate grassland of South Africa is called…
questions.x: Veld (South Africa), Pampas (Argentina), Steppe (Eurasia), Downs (Australia), Prairies (North America).

questions.q: On which date is the longest day in India?
questions.x: On 21 June the Sun is over the Tropic of Cancer, so the northern half has its longest day.

questions.q: Sea animals that live on the sea floor are called…
questions.x: Benthos live on the floor; plankton drift; nekton swim freely.
